Issue Description: The check 'nullptr != _libUSBDeviceThread' after 'new std::thread(...)' is unreachable dead code. In C++, 'new' either returns a valid non-null pointer or throws std::bad_alloc; it never returns nullptr. The nullptr branch is therefore never taken.
Suggested Fix: Remove the dead nullptr check and replace with a try/catch around the 'new std::thread' call to handle std::bad_alloc, setting _handlingUSBDeviceEvents to false on exception.
Resolution Status and Notes: Fixed - replaced dead nullptr check with try/catch(std::bad_alloc) around the new std::thread call

Source Code Snippet: auto len = fileFrom.Read(buffer, bufLen); if (len <= 0) { break; }
Issue Description: The Read() method likely returns uint32_t (unsigned). Comparing an unsigned value with <= 0 means the negative branch (len < 0) is unreachable. Only the '== 0' case triggers a break, but code readability and intent are misleading.
Suggested Fix: Change the check to 'if (len == 0) { break; }' to correctly reflect that an unsigned return value of 0 means no bytes were read.
Resolution Status and Notes: Fixed - changed len <= 0 to len == 0 for unsigned type correctness
